lessons.title: Reading: a fossil discovery in Brazil
lessons.subtitle: Leitura: pistas sobre a origem dos dinossauros
lessons.intro:
A fossil is evidence. Read what was found, where it was found and what scientists can learn from it.

Um fóssil é uma evidência. Leia o que foi encontrado, onde e o que os cientistas podem aprender.

facts.term: A very old reptile / Um réptil muito antigo
facts.text:
The school reading describes Gondwanax paraisensis, a small reptile with a long tail that lived about 237 million years ago, during the Triassic Period. It compares the animal with a small dog in size. This is a comparison of size, not a claim that it was a dog.

O texto escolar descreve Gondwanax paraisensis, um pequeno réptil de cauda longa que viveu há cerca de 237 milhões de anos, no período Triássico. Compara o tamanho do animal ao de um cachorro pequeno; isso não significa que ele fosse um cachorro.

facts.term: Discovery and study / Descoberta e estudo
facts.text:
Pedro Lucas Porcela Aurélio found the fossil in Paraíso do Sul, in southern Brazil. The material was donated to CAPPA at the Federal University of Santa Maria. Paleontologist Rodrigo Temp Müller studied the bones. The finder and the researcher had different roles.

Pedro Lucas Porcela Aurélio encontrou o fóssil em Paraíso do Sul, no sul do Brasil. O material foi doado ao CAPPA da Universidade Federal de Santa Maria. O paleontólogo Rodrigo Temp Müller estudou os ossos. Quem encontrou e quem pesquisou tiveram papéis diferentes.

facts.term: What can the evidence tell us? / O que a evidência revela?
facts.text:
The fossil belongs to a group called silesaurids. Scientists debate whether these animals were early dinosaurs or very close relatives. Comparing their bones can help explain the origin and early evolution of dinosaurs. The reading presents a question being investigated, not proof that every ancient reptile was a dinosaur.

O fóssil pertence a um grupo chamado silessaurídeos. Cientistas discutem se eram dinossauros primitivos ou parentes muito próximos. Comparar os ossos ajuda a entender a origem e a evolução inicial dos dinossauros. O texto apresenta uma questão em investigação, não uma prova de que todo réptil antigo era dinossauro.

lessons.remember:
Evidence helps us investigate. It does not answer every question at once.

Evidências ajudam a investigar. Elas não respondem a todas as perguntas de uma vez.

lessons.title: Reading: Hurricane Matthew
lessons.subtitle: Leitura: observe, compare e explique
lessons.intro:
Hurricane Matthew affected Haiti and other places in 2016. Strong winds, heavy rain and waves changed landscapes. Compare evidence from before and after.

O furacão Matthew atingiu o Haiti e outros lugares em 2016. Ventos fortes, chuva intensa e ondas mudaram paisagens. Compare evidências de antes e depois.

facts.term: Haiti from space / Haiti visto do espaço
facts.text:
The satellite images near the Cavaillon River show more green vegetation before the hurricane and browner land afterwards. Damage to vegetation and sediment carried by water help explain the change. Green loss is an observation; explaining its cause requires the reading and other evidence.

As imagens de satélite próximas ao rio Cavaillon mostram mais vegetação verde antes do furacão e terreno mais amarronzado depois. Danos à vegetação e sedimentos transportados pela água ajudam a explicar a mudança. A perda de verde é uma observação; explicar a causa exige o texto e outras evidências.

facts.term: Dunes on the coast / Dunas no litoral
facts.text:
A separate before-and-after photograph in the material shows a new opening through a sand dune near St. Augustine, Florida, USA. Storm waves moved sand and opened a connection between the ocean and the estuary. These USGS dune photographs are from Florida; they are not satellite photographs of Haiti.

Outra comparação do material mostra uma abertura nova numa duna próxima de St. Augustine, na Flórida, EUA. Ondas da tempestade transportaram areia e abriram uma ligação entre o oceano e o estuário. Essas fotos de dunas do USGS são da Flórida; não são imagens de satélite do Haiti.

facts.term: Connect the processes / Relacione os processos
facts.text:
Weathering breaks or changes rock in place. Erosion removes and transports material. Deposition leaves that material in a new place. Water carrying soil or waves carrying sand are examples of erosion. When the transported material settles, deposition happens. A storm can cause rapid natural changes. People also change landscapes through farming and construction.

O intemperismo fragmenta ou altera rochas no local. A erosão remove e transporta material. A deposição deixa esse material em um novo lugar. Água levando solo ou ondas levando areia são exemplos de erosão. Quando o material transportado se acumula, ocorre deposição. Uma tempestade pode causar mudanças naturais rápidas. Pessoas também mudam paisagens com agricultura e construção.

lessons.remember:
Observe first. Explain with evidence. Keep the place and date of each image together.

Observe primeiro. Explique com evidências. Mantenha o local e a data de cada imagem juntos.

s3-fossil-discovery.example:
Where? Paraíso do Sul. When did the animal live? About 237 million years ago. Why study it? To investigate early dinosaur evolution.

Onde? Paraíso do Sul. Quando o animal viveu? Há cerca de 237 milhões de anos. Por que estudá-lo? Para investigar a evolução inicial dos dinossauros.

paragraphs:

s3-rock-types.term: Examples and uses / Exemplos e usos
s3-rock-types.text:
Igneous: granite for buildings, basalt for roads, pumice as an abrasive. Sedimentary: sandstone for buildings and limestone for cement. Metamorphic: marble for sculptures and slate for roofing. Granite and rhyolite can form from similar magma but have different textures because of cooling rates. Devils Tower is made of phonolite porphyry, an igneous rock.

Ígneas: granito em construções, basalto em estradas e pedra-pomes como abrasivo. Sedimentares: arenito em construções e calcário na produção de cimento. Metamórficas: mármore em esculturas e ardósia em telhados. Granito e riolito podem se formar de magma semelhante, mas apresentam texturas diferentes pela velocidade de resfriamento. Devils Tower é formado por fonolito porfirítico, uma rocha ígnea.

s3-landscapes.text:
A cliff is a steep rock face; a canyon is a deep valley with steep sides. A mesa has a broad flat top and steep sides; a butte is smaller. An isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining larger areas. A delta forms where a river deposits sediment. Dunes are hills of sand; a glacier is a large mass of ice moving slowly. A canal in the school guide is human-made, not a natural landform.

Uma falésia é uma face rochosa íngreme; um cânion é um vale profundo de lados íngremes. Uma mesa tem topo plano amplo e lados íngremes; um butte é menor. Um istmo é uma faixa estreita de terra unindo áreas maiores. Um delta se forma onde um rio deposita sedimentos. Dunas são montes de areia; uma geleira é uma grande massa de gelo que se move lentamente. O canal do guia escolar é construído pelas pessoas, não uma forma natural do relevo.

s3-rocks-minerals.term: More mineral uses / Mais usos dos minerais
s3-rocks-minerals.text:
Calcite is a main mineral in natural chalk. Halite is the mineral form of common salt. Some drawing materials use mineral pigments or fillers. Quartz helps clocks keep time; it is not a battery that powers them. Graphite in a pencil is not the metal lead.

Calcita é um dos principais minerais do giz natural. Halita é a forma mineral do sal comum. Alguns materiais de desenho usam pigmentos ou cargas minerais. Quartzo ajuda relógios a marcar o tempo; não é uma bateria que fornece energia. O grafite do lápis não é o metal chumbo.

practice.prompt: Give four natural and four artificial sound examples. Classify by source. / Dê quatro exemplos de cada origem.
practice.answer: Natural: birds, rain, thunder, flowing water. Artificial: alarm, car horn, phone, loudspeaker. Other justified examples are acceptable.

practice.prompt: Explain pitch, volume and echo. Can a sound be high-pitched and quiet? / Explique altura, intensidade e eco.
practice.answer: Pitch depends on vibration rate; volume on vibration size; echo is reflected sound. Yes: a whistle played softly can be high-pitched and quiet.

practice.prompt: Put in order: brain; cochlea; ear canal; tiny bones; eardrum; auditory nerve. / Ordene o caminho da audição.
practice.answer: Ear canal → eardrum → tiny bones → cochlea → auditory nerve → brain. The outer ear helps collect incoming waves.

practice.prompt: Explain the jobs of the eardrum, cochlea and auditory nerve. / Explique a função de cada parte.
practice.answer: Eardrum vibrates. The cochlea helps change vibrations into nerve signals. The auditory nerve carries signals to the brain, which interprets them.

practice.prompt: Explain rock versus mineral. Name three minerals and one use for each. / Diferencie e dê exemplos com usos.
practice.answer: A rock contains one or more minerals. A mineral is a natural solid with characteristic composition and structure. Quartz: timekeeping; graphite: pencils; diamond: jewellery.

practice.prompt: Granite contains quartz, feldspar and mica. Which is the rock? List three properties used to describe minerals. / Identifique a rocha e as propriedades.
practice.answer: Granite is the rock; quartz, feldspar and mica are minerals. Colour, hardness and shine are examples of properties.

practice.prompt: Compare intrusive and extrusive igneous rocks. Give three igneous examples and uses. / Compare e dê exemplos.
practice.answer: Intrusive: slower cooling underground, often larger crystals. Extrusive: faster cooling at the surface, usually smaller crystals. Granite: buildings; basalt: roads; pumice: abrasive.

practice.prompt: Explain sedimentary and metamorphic formation. Give two examples and uses of each, and complete: limestone → __; shale → __; granite → __.
practice.answer: Sedimentary: accumulated sediments, often compacted and cemented; sandstone: building; limestone: cement. Metamorphic: heat/pressure without wholesale melting; marble: sculpture; slate: roofing. Transformations: marble, slate, gneiss.

practice.prompt: Explain what fossils are, where they are often found and how some form. / Explique fósseis, ocorrência e formação.
practice.answer: Preserved remains or traces of ancient life, often in sedimentary rocks. Remains may be buried by sediment; layers accumulate and minerals may fill or replace material over time. Not every organism becomes a fossil.

practice.prompt: Why are fossils useful? Give a fossil example that is not a dinosaur bone. / Explique a importância e dê outro exemplo.
practice.answer: They provide evidence of past life and environments. Examples include a fossil leaf, shell or footprint. Accept other valid remains or traces.

practice.prompt: Describe a landscape with two natural and two human-made features. Name five landforms. / Descreva uma paisagem e cite formas de relevo.
practice.answer: Example: mountains and a river, with a bridge and houses. Landforms: mountain, valley, plateau, island, peninsula. Other accurate examples are accepted.

practice.prompt: Compare island/peninsula and valley/plateau. Is a constructed canal a natural landform? Explain. / Compare as formas.
practice.answer: Island: surrounded by water; peninsula: connected to larger land. Valley: low between higher land; plateau: elevated with a relatively flat top. A constructed canal is human-made.

practice.prompt: Classify and explain: ice splits a rock; a river carries fragments; sand settles at a river mouth. / Classifique as três situações.
practice.answer: Weathering: breaking in place. Erosion/transport: river carries fragments. Deposition: transported sand settles.

practice.prompt: Describe how roots and freezing water can break rocks. Then explain how wind can move the pieces. / Explique os processos.
practice.answer: Growing roots widen cracks. Water expands when it freezes in cracks. Wind can carry loose particles away: erosion/transport follows or accompanies weathering.

practice.prompt: List five ways to reduce soil erosion. Explain two. / Cite cinco métodos e explique dois.
practice.answer: Vegetation, ground cover/mulch, barriers, terraces, cover crops. Roots hold soil; cover shields it; barriers and terraces slow runoff. Cover crops protect otherwise bare fields.

practice.prompt: A field on a slope loses soil in heavy rain. Propose two measures and explain how they help. / Proponha duas medidas.
practice.answer: For example, terraces reduce runoff speed and cover crops help hold and shield soil. Accept other justified methods from the lesson; no method guarantees zero erosion.

practice.prompt: Read the fossil text. Identify the animal, place, approximate age and geological period. / Identifique os quatro dados.
practice.answer: Gondwanax paraisensis; Paraíso do Sul, southern Brazil; about 237 million years ago; Triassic Period.

practice.prompt: Who found the fossil? Who studied it? Why is it important, and what question remains debated? / Explique os papéis e a importância.
practice.answer: Pedro Lucas Porcela Aurélio found it; Rodrigo Temp Müller studied it at UFSM/CAPPA. It offers clues to early dinosaur evolution. Whether silesaurids were early dinosaurs or close relatives remains debated in the reading.

practice.prompt: Compare the Haiti images with the Florida account in the lesson. Describe a change in each place. / Compare as imagens do Haiti com o relato da Flórida.
practice.answer: Haiti: less green vegetation and more brown/sediment-rich areas after the storm. Florida: a new inlet/gap through the dune. Do not identify the Florida dune photographs as Haiti.

practice.prompt: Explain how Matthew changed the landscape using erosion and deposition. Suggest one way vegetation helps protect soil. / Use os conceitos.
practice.answer: Water and waves removed and transported soil/sand: erosion. Sediment accumulated elsewhere: deposition. Vegetation helps hold soil with roots and shields the surface. A storm is a natural agent; its impacts can be rapid.
